title: Year 9 retrieval quiz
subject: English
unit: Summer 2: Year 9 mastery and readiness for the International GCSE
source: Seeded from english/y9 lesson 67 (Year 9 retrieval quiz (portal))
intro: Covers lessons 67 to 82 of Year 9 mastery and readiness for the International GCSE. Answer every question. For multiple choice, fill in one circle.

questions.q: Which is a conceptual thesis about Macbeth?
options: Shakespeare presents ambition as a force that destroys the conscience it feeds on.
Macbeth is a play by Shakespeare.
questions.a: A) Shakespeare presents ambition as a force that destroys the conscience it feeds on.. It argues about a big idea; the others state facts.

questions.q: Why is it significant that Piggy's glasses are stolen rather than simply broken?
options: Jack takes the power of fire and reason for himself
questions.a: B) Jack takes the power of fire and reason for himself. Stealing them shows power being seized; the means to make fire now belongs to the hunters.

questions.q: Which evidence best supports 'Macbeth is a victim'?
options: the witches' prophecies and Lady Macbeth's pressure
questions.a: C) the witches' prophecies and Lady Macbeth's pressure. Outside influences support the victim reading; the other actions are his own choices.

questions.q: Which connective best introduces a difference?
questions.a: A) Whereas. Whereas signals contrast; the others signal similarity or addition.

questions.q: For the Macbeth question, the strongest opening is...
options: a conceptual thesis that answers the question
a summary of the whole play
questions.a: B) a conceptual thesis that answers the question. A thesis answers the question and guides the essay.

questions.q: Q5 is an evaluation. What must your answer include?
options: a new story of your own
a judgement supported by evidence from the text
questions.a: C) a judgement supported by evidence from the text. Evaluation means judging how far you agree, with evidence.

questions.q: What should your first paragraph do?
options: state a thesis and analyse the extract
questions.a: A) state a thesis and analyse the extract. Start with your argument and the extract, then move to the wider play.

questions.q: Which plan is strongest for Task B?
options: A small moment, one setting, a change, an ending that echoes the first line
questions.a: B) A small moment, one setting, a change, an ending that echoes the first line. A short story works best with a small focus and a clear shape.

questions.q: Which sentence best summarises the text?
options: Volunteers helped a polluted river recover.
questions.a: C) Volunteers helped a polluted river recover.. It captures the whole text, not one detail.

questions.q: Which semantic field runs through the extract?
questions.a: A) war and invasion. invaded, marched, columns, surrender all belong to war.

questions.q: Why does the ending repeat the opening with 'and the boy' added?
options: to show the same place now holds his story
because the writer ran out of ideas
questions.a: B) to show the same place now holds his story. The echo makes us look at the station again, now aware of the boy's mystery.

questions.q: Which feedback is most useful?
options: Zoom in on 'fragile' to explain its effect.
questions.a: C) Zoom in on 'fragile' to explain its effect.. It names one specific, actionable improvement.

questions.q: Which uses context best?
options: Jacobean audiences believed guilt revealed God's judgement, so her collapse feels inevitable.
Macbeth was written a long time ago.
questions.a: A) Jacobean audiences believed guilt revealed God's judgement, so her collapse feels inevitable.. It connects context to an interpretation of the text.

questions.q: Which redraft is strongest for 'I felt sad when I saw it.'?
options: I was sad and upset and unhappy.
I did not open it at first.
questions.a: B) I did not open it at first.. Showing hesitation through action is more powerful than naming the feeling.

questions.q: Which section asks you to use ideas from the reading texts in your own writing?
questions.a: C) Section B. Section B is directed writing based on the texts.

questions.q: Which part is closed book?
questions.a: A) Component 1. Component 1 (poetry and modern prose) is closed book.

questions.q: In Lord of the Flies, the conch represents...
questions.a: B) order and democracy

questions.q: Who says 'Fair is foul, and foul is fair'?
questions.a: B) the witches

questions.q: Arthur Kipps travels to...
questions.a: B) Eel Marsh House

questions.q: A conceptual thesis argues about...
questions.a: C) a big idea
